html:
León Viejo is the ruin of the first Spanish city of León in Nicaragua, founded in 1524 on Lake Managua below the volcano Momotombo. Its people abandoned it after an earthquake in 1610.

It was the seat of the colonial governors and of the first bishop. Its founder, Francisco Hernández de Córdoba, was beheaded there by his superior Pedrarias Dávila, whose own tomb was found in the ruins. The town traded in Native slaves sent to Peru during the conquest.

After the earthquake the people moved west and founded the new León, which became the liberal and university city of Nicaragua and the rival of conservative Granada. The buried old town was found in 1967 and became a World Heritage Site in 2000. It is one of the oldest Spanish towns in the Americas, alongside Santo Domingo.
